question.:question/worked-solution:
We proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to \infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{\infty }\frac{482}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{3}^{a}\frac{482}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =482{lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{3}^{a}{x}^{-4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =482{lim}_{a\to \infty }{[(-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{-3})]}_{3}^{a} \\  & =-\frac{482}{3}\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{[\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}]}_{3}^{a} \\  & =-\frac{482}{3}\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }(\frac{1}{{a}^{3}}-\frac{1}{{3}^{3}}) \\  & =-\frac{482}{3}(0-\frac{1}{27}) \\  & =\frac{482}{81}.\end{aligned}
$$
